The supplied passages affect the following people and Office roles:

1. **People seeking extensions of time.** Under the **Act**, s 224(1) requires the Registrar to extend time where the specified Office-side error or omission prevents timely performance of a relevant act. Section 224(2) permits an extension on an application by the person concerned in accordance with the Regulations. [TMA1995/s224]

2. **Potential opponents seeking more time to file opposition documents.** The **Manual practice** requires an approved-form application, the relevant fee and a supporting declaration for an extension to file a notice of intention to oppose or statement of grounds and particulars. Processing waits until payment. The trade mark applicant is also affected: the Registrar gives that applicant a copy of the request. [TMM/Part49/2/2/3/2]

3. **Trade mark applicants approaching the lapsing date after an examination delay.** The **Manual practice** says an examiner may indicate that an applicant can request an extension equivalent to the delay near the lapsing date; a free extension is not automatic. [TMM/Part15/1/1/1]

4. **People opposing an extension, and the extension applicant.** The **Act** permits a person to oppose the granting of the application as prescribed. The **Regulations** define a party in this Division as an applicant or opponent. The **Manual practice** specifies an approved-form notice, a one-month non-extendible filing period and payment of the relevant fee, with a copy sent to the extension applicant. [TMA1995/s224(6); TMR1995/r21.20A; TMM/Part15/6/6/2]

5. **People seeking late costs awards or filing late bills of costs.** The **Manual practice** says consideration requires an extension under s 224, sought in an approved form with the appropriate fee and supporting declaration. [TMM/Part55/3/3/4]

6. **Extension applicants and other parties involved in hearings.** The **Manual practice** provides an opportunity to request a hearing where the delegate intends to refuse the specified opposition-document extension. The request requires a fee; if a hearing is scheduled, both parties can be heard in national trade mark oppositions. [TMM/Part47/1/1/3/6~2]

7. **The Registrar and Office personnel administering these processes.** The Registrar has the statutory extension functions noted above. Under **Manual practice**, TM&D Administration enters a paid opposition notice, preventing system processing of the extension, and forwards it to the Hearings Support Unit. [TMA1995/s224; TMM/Part15/6/6/2]

**Limit:** The legislation list names general lapsing and non-complying-document provisions but does not reproduce their rules. The supplied material therefore does not establish the complete scope of who is affected by those provisions. [TMM/Part15/x-relevant-legislation13#1]"}
